decisions.question: OQ-F1: which router do the Flutter executor and the module binding target: Flutter's own Navigator and Router APIs, or go_router as Guide §3.4 shows, and does that router become a dependency of the adapter?

options.label: Flutter Navigator, no router dependency
options.consequence: The adapter depends on Flutter alone; the router keeps its own stack, applies performs synchronously and confirms before perform returns; apps on go_router implement navigation-api@v1's NavigationRouter themselves; no web URL sync in v1.

options.label: go_router as a dependency
options.consequence: Matches Guide §3.4's example and gives URL routing, but the published adapter would carry material_ui, cupertino_ui, flutter_localizations and intl; push lands a frame later, there is no pop-until, go has route-tree semantics that contradict navigation-api@v1 Refinement 7, and go_router handles the platform's initial route itself, past the bus guard.

options.label: Navigator now, plus a go_router NavigationRouter package in v1
options.consequence: Serves both kinds of app, but adds a package and a node-level deliverable root D1 does not schedule.

decisions.why: The experiment settled the facts: Navigator calls reach observers synchronously (P2), so a router over Navigator can meet navigation-api@v1 G18 exactly (26 of 26 executor cases under testWidgets); go_router's push reaches the Navigator only after a frame (R2), it has no popUntil (R3), it navigates to the platform's initial route by itself (R4), go turns [/, /a] into [/, /b] (R5), and 18.x pulls material and cupertino packages (R1). navigation-api@v1 Refinement 7 already rejected go's semantics for GoTo, and ADR-002 adds a router package only if this question selects one. Not a tree-shape stop: both options produce the same nodes and the same contract set. The signal that would have changed my mind: an owner-named v1 app that needs web URL synchronization or is already on go_router.

decisions.question: Settle the bootstrap: NavigationExecutor reads router.stack when constructed, so either the Navigator is mounted first, or the router accepts calls before mount.

options.label: Router accepts performs before mount
options.consequence: Guide §3.5's order (resolver, executor, start(), runApp) works unchanged; the router keeps its stack and the hosting Navigator starts from it.

options.label: Navigator mounted before the executor is constructed
options.consequence: The executor and start() must wait for the first frame; a deep link queued before start() needs the bootstrap to defer start() into a post-frame callback.

decisions.why: runApp attaches the root widget from a Timer, so the microtasks in which start()'s reentrant deliveries reach the executor run while no Navigator exists (P1); the second option would reorder Guide §3.5's bootstrap for every app. G12 and G16 state and test it.

decisions.question: Which routes hold a module scope reference: every route on the Navigator's stack whose path matches, or only the visible top route?

options.label: Stack membership
options.consequence: A module stays active while any of its routes is on the stack, covered or not; its covered pages keep their module-owned state alive.

options.label: Top route only
options.consequence: A module is released when another module's route covers it, and reactivated on return; covered pages, still mounted, read state whose owner is gone.

decisions.why: Flutter keeps covered routes mounted (P3), so their PAGE topologies stay active, and Spec §7.2 requires a state topic's owner to live at least as long as its readers. Spec §7.3 says module scope ends when navigation leaves the subtree and is silent on stacked navigators, so the reading is a clarification worth upstreaming. The signal that would have changed my mind: an owner requirement to tear down covered modules for memory.

decisions.question: When is a popped route's module reference released: at didPop, or when the route is disposed after its exit transition?

options.label: At didPop
options.consequence: Follows Spec §7.3's push and pop binding; the grace period covers the exit transition.

options.label: At route disposal
options.consequence: Tracks the page's real lifetime, but NavigatorObserver has no disposal callback, so it needs per-route hooks the app's route builder would have to install.

decisions.why: Spec §7.3 binds the reference to route push and pop and makes the grace period configurable for slow transition animations; P6 shows observers get no disposal notice.

decisions.question: On a route replacement inside a module's subtree, in which order are references acquired and released?

options.label: Acquire new, then release old
options.consequence: The count never crosses zero, so even a zero grace period keeps the topologies.

options.label: Release old, then acquire new
options.consequence: With a zero grace period the topologies tear down and reactivate on every in-subtree replace.

decisions.why: Spec §7.3 item 2: an in-subtree navigation balances the count without crossing zero. P2 shows pushReplacement reports didReplace, so the observer sees both routes in one callback.

decisions.question: What does the module observer do when an acquire throws (bus-api@v1 G28 rethrows an activation failure)?

options.label: Report through FlutterError.reportError
options.consequence: The error surfaces in debug runs and tests (takeException); the route holds no reference; the Navigator keeps working.

options.label: Rethrow into the Navigator
options.consequence: The exception escapes the Navigator's observer notification and leaves the Navigator locked: later operations fail the '!_debugLocked' assertion.

decisions.why: Found by experiment: the first version of the suite threw ActivationRejected from didPush, and the Navigator then failed '!_debugLocked' assertions at unmount. Reporting matches how Flutter itself reports observer errors.

decisions.question: Two mounted PageScopes that name one topology id (one route pushed twice): how is the shared handle released?

options.label: Count holders per bus and topology id
options.consequence: The topology lives until the last mounted scope naming it unmounts.

options.label: Activate and deactivate per mount
options.consequence: The first unmount deactivates the shared handle (bus-api@v1 G25) and the page below loses its topology.

options.label: Reject a second mount
options.consequence: A route pushed twice fails to mount.

decisions.chosen: Count holders per bus and topology id
decisions.why: Activation is idempotent and returns one handle (Spec §3.9, bus-api@v1 G23), whose deactivation ends the topology for every holder (G25). Spec §7.3's React StrictMode note asks adapters to offset a duplicate mount the same way for modules; Spec §7.1 is silent for pages, so it is marked for upstreaming. A bus-api@v1 'page scope' primitive would move the count into the runtime; not needed for v1.

decisions.question: Does a PageScope rebind when rebuilt with other arguments (route, topologies, writes)?

options.label: Bind once, at mount
options.consequence: Simple and ordering-free; a new key remounts it.

options.label: Rebind on change
options.consequence: Follows argument changes, but must order the old publisher's release, the new claims and the topology counts, and a claim conflict mid-rebind leaves half a binding.

decisions.why: No evidence that pages change these arguments in place; the Flutter idiom for initial-only arguments is a new key. The signal that would have changed my mind: a page whose route argument changes without a remount.

decisions.question: How does a topic widget render: read getCurrentValue at every build with the subscription only invalidating, or keep the observed values in its State?

options.label: Render the bus's current value; subscription only invalidates
options.consequence: No copy of the value exists to drift; the first frame needs no delivery; a parent rebuild always renders the latest value.

options.label: Keep observed values in State
options.consequence: A second state holder between topic and UI, the drift Rationale §5.2 item 3 warns of, and the first value must still come from getCurrentValue.

decisions.chosen: Render the bus's current value; subscription only invalidates
decisions.why: Rationale §5.1 and §5.2 (no interposed state holder), Spec §2.5 (getCurrentValue as the synchronous first read), Guide §7.2's useSyncExternalStore pattern, and bus-api@v1 G17 (the first observed value is the value current at listen, so skipping it renders nothing twice).

decisions.question: How does an app say whether a BusProvider owns, and so shuts down, its bus?

options.label: Unnamed constructor owns, BusProvider.value does not
options.consequence: Follows the provider package's .value convention Guide §6.4's Provider<Bus> implies; the root case is the short form.

options.label: A boolean flag
options.consequence: One constructor; a flag defaulting either way hides the shutdown decision.

options.label: A separate lifetime widget
options.consequence: Two widgets to place in the right order for every app and test.

decisions.chosen: Unnamed constructor owns, BusProvider.value does not
decisions.why: Guide §6.4 names Provider<Bus>; in that package .value never disposes. ADR-003 item 7 needs a widget above every scope binding that shuts the bus down at unmount, which the owning provider at the root is.

decisions.question: What ends the coordination domain on Flutter: the owning provider's dispose only, or also AppLifecycleState.detached?

options.label: Owning provider's dispose only
options.consequence: Tests, closed views and torn-down add-to-app views shut down; a mobile process that is killed does not, which is unobservable.

options.label: Also AppLifecycleState.detached
options.consequence: Closer to Spec §11.2's iOS trigger, but detached is entered whenever every view detaches while the engine runs on, so a cached engine that reattaches finds a bus that cannot restart.

decisions.why: The SDK documents detached as 'still hosted by a Flutter engine but detached from any host views', a state the app can leave again; Spec §11.2's table has no Flutter row, so the mapping is marked for upstreaming. An owner who wants shutdown on process end on iOS would decide otherwise.

decisions.question: Platform routes (the initial route and routes the platform pushes): who turns them into intents?

options.label: The executor forwards them as DeepLink, on by default
options.consequence: No route is ever pushed by name over the router; Guide §3.5's capture works out of the box; an app with its own deep-link capture turns it off.

options.label: Left to the app
options.consequence: A Navigator-based WidgetsApp pushes a platform route by name through onGenerateRoute (P5), which the router cannot represent and which bypasses the guard.

options.label: Opt-in forwarding
options.consequence: Safe only when the app remembers it.

decisions.chosen: The executor forwards them as DeepLink, on by default
decisions.why: P5 shows WidgetsApp pushes a platform route by name unless an earlier binding observer answers it; P5b shows the observer must be registered before WidgetsApp mounts, which Guide §3.5's order gives. The Owns list names the executor, not deep-link capture, so a careful engineer would have confirmed the scope.

decisions.question: Which settings does a router route carry, and who builds the Flutter route?

options.label: App builds the route from (entry, settings); settings named '/' + path carrying the entry; other settings rejected
options.consequence: Apps choose MaterialPageRoute, Cupertino or dialogs; the observer and page source read the entry; web and the engine see an absolute route name.

options.label: Adapter builds a PageRouteBuilder around an app widget builder
options.consequence: Less app code, but no Material or Cupertino transitions without depending on those libraries.

options.label: Name equal to the path, no leading slash
options.consequence: Matches NavRoute.path, but WidgetsApp reports the top route's name to the engine as a URI, where a relative name is wrong.

decisions.chosen: App builds the route from (entry, settings); settings named '/' + path carrying the entry; other settings rejected
decisions.why: WidgetsApp's Navigator reports route names to the engine (reportsRouteUpdateToEngine), and Flutter route names conventionally begin with '/'; the settings check makes the observer's pathOf and the page source reliable.

decisions.question: How does the router treat routes it did not build (dialogs, sheets, app pushes)?

options.label: Not entries; a perform pops the ones above the top entry first
options.consequence: Their push and pop confirm nothing; after a perform the top entry's route is the Navigator's top.

options.label: Treat them as entries
options.consequence: They have no NavigationEntry to confirm.

options.label: Remove them silently with removeRoute
options.consequence: Skips their pop transitions and leaves their futures to complete unusually.

decisions.chosen: Not entries; a perform pops the ones above the top entry first
decisions.why: P7 shows a dialog is an observed push of an unnamed route and popUntil on a route identity pops it; navigation-api@v1 G18 confirms only stack changes.

decisions.question: The executor's default name.

options.label: flutter-navigation
options.consequence: Its source renders executor:flutter-navigation, as Spec §2.4's example and Guide §3.4 show.

options.label: navigation
options.consequence: NavigationExecutor's own default; two platforms' executors would share one source.

decisions.why: Spec §2.4's example publisher is 'executor:flutter-navigation'.

decisions.question: What does the widget-test library offer, given it may import neither test framework and so takes no WidgetTester?

options.label: WidgetTestBus: bus, recorder, input, stub, wrap
options.consequence: Mirrors TestBus's input and stub with ServiceSource('test'), so tests read alike on the VM and in widgets; wrap's owning provider does the ADR-003 item 7 shutdown.

options.label: Only a wrap helper
options.consequence: Every widget test re-creates recorder and stub plumbing.

options.label: A pump helper taking a WidgetTester
options.consequence: Needs package:flutter_test, which ADR-002 item 4 forbids.

decisions.chosen: WidgetTestBus: bus, recorder, input, stub, wrap
decisions.why: ADR-002 item 4, ADR-003 item 7 and bus-testing@v1 G18 and 'How a test uses it'. It rejects a VirtualSchedulerProvider because tester.pump would not move its clock (ADR-003 item 7).

decisions.question: What is the module-scope binding mechanism on Flutter?

options.label: A NavigatorObserver subclass
options.consequence: Sees push, pop, remove and replace on any Navigator; needs nothing of RouteObserver's RouteAware subscriptions.

options.label: A RouteObserver subclass
options.consequence: The Spec's word, but its added API (RouteAware subscribe) is unused here.

options.label: A wrapper widget on the subtree, as React does
options.consequence: Contradicts Spec §7.3's Flutter row.

decisions.why: Spec §7.3's Flutter row is 'RouteObserver plus a route prefix match'; RouteObserver is itself a NavigatorObserver, and the binding needs only the observer callbacks.

decisions.question: How does a module prefix match a route path?

options.label: By segments, ignoring a leading '/' and empty segments
options.consequence: 'checkout' matches 'checkout/cart' and '/checkout', not 'checkouts'.

options.label: By string prefix
options.consequence: 'checkout' matches 'checkouts' and fails on a leading '/'.

decisions.chosen: By segments, ignoring a leading '/' and empty segments
decisions.why: Router routes are named '/' + path and app routes usually begin with '/'; a string prefix gives false matches.

decisions.question: A Navigator that unmounts reports no pop of its routes (P6): how are its module references released?

options.label: ModuleScopeObserver.dispose
options.consequence: An app that removes a Navigator for good disposes its observer; the root Navigator ends with the bus, whose shutdown deactivates every scope.

options.label: Nothing
options.consequence: References of a removed nested Navigator leak and keep their modules active.

decisions.why: P6: after unmount the observer's navigator is null and no didPop or didRemove arrived.

decisions.question: Which conveniences does v1 leave out?

options.label: Leave out Router-widget integration and web URL sync, nested-Navigator executors, an event-topic listener widget, a BuildContext extension, route restoration
options.consequence: A smaller surface to fixture now; each is a compatible addition later.

options.label: Include them
options.consequence: More surface and fixtures, with no v1 consumer named.

decisions.chosen: Leave out Router-widget integration and web URL sync, nested-Navigator executors, an event-topic listener widget, a BuildContext extension, route restoration
decisions.why: The Owns list names neither; root D1 names no web target. The owner may want web URL sync, which is the item a careful engineer would have asked about.

decisions.question: Which Flutter libraries may the main library import?

options.label: widgets, foundation and services only
options.consequence: Material, Cupertino and custom-design apps all use it without pulling a design library.

options.label: material too
options.consequence: MaterialPageRoute defaults inside the adapter, at the cost of the material dependency for every app.

decisions.why: The app's route builder chooses the presentation; material_ui and cupertino_ui are now pub packages (pub.dev, as go_router 18 depends on them), so the design libraries are moving out of the core.

decisions.question: What does the contract say about app code that removes or replaces router routes itself?

options.label: Outside the contract; no guarantee
options.consequence: Honest and small; a dev-mode diagnostic stays a v2 candidate.

options.label: Report a dev-mode diagnostic
options.consequence: Needs the router to reach the bus, which it does not hold.

options.label: Resynchronize the stack
options.consequence: There is no intent to confirm such a change with.

decisions.why: navigation-api@v1's confirmations carry an intent, and no intent describes an external removal.

decisions.question: One page widget for topologies and publisher, or two?

options.label: One PageScope with topologies and a publisher
options.consequence: A page binds its scope in one place; the publisher can claim page-scoped state.

options.label: Separate PageTopologies and PagePublisher widgets
options.consequence: Finer control, two widgets to order per page.

decisions.chosen: One PageScope with topologies and a publisher
decisions.why: Spec §2.4: a publisher bound to a page scope releases its claim with that scope; Spec §5.2 treats a page as one shell component with a topology and publishes.

decisions.question: In the executor suite's Flutter binding, is the executor constructed before or after the hosting WidgetsApp is pumped (S12's template pumps first)?

options.label: Construct, then pump
options.consequence: Exercises the production order of Guide §3.5 and G12 in every case.

options.label: Pump, then construct
options.consequence: S12's template; never exercises a router performing before mount.

decisions.why: G12 makes construction before mount the supported order, and P1 shows production reaches the executor before any Navigator exists; both orders pass, this one covers more.

decisions.question: How do the bindings perform the platform's back?

options.label: The navigation channel's popRoute message
options.consequence: The real path: binding, WidgetsApp.didPopRoute, Navigator.maybePop, PopScope included.

options.label: navigatorKey.currentState.maybePop()
options.consequence: S12's template; skips WidgetsApp and the binding.

options.label: binding.handlePopRoute()
options.consequence: @protected and @visibleForTesting, so an analyzer diagnostic in a fixture.

decisions.why: P4 shows popRoute through WidgetsApp pops the top route, never the root, and honors PopScope.

decisions.question: How does a conformance library that imports no flutter_test observe the tree?

options.label: Harness methods for the tester's operations; cases observe through their own widgets, builder callbacks and NavigatorObservers
options.consequence: No finder types cross the harness; the suite stays bindable under any runner that can pump.

options.label: Expose finders through the harness
options.consequence: Leaks flutter_test types into the harness interface.

decisions.chosen: Harness methods for the tester's operations; cases observe through their own widgets, builder callbacks and NavigatorObservers
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4: a conformance library imports neither test package; earlier contracts' harnesses abstract time and runner the same way.

experiments.question: OQ-F1's runtime facts (Navigator observer timing, runApp's attach, platform back and route push, unmount, dialogs; go_router's push timing, pop-until, initial route, go semantics and dependencies), and whether flutter-binding@v1's fixtures and navigation-api@v1's executor suite run against a stand-in of the Interface under fvm flutter test from a pure-Dart workspace root.
experiments.finding: Navigator: observer callbacks run synchronously inside push, pushReplacement (reported as didReplace), replace, pop and popUntil (P2); the initial routes are reported as pushes, bottom first, and covered routes stay mounted (P3); a platform popRoute pops the top route through WidgetsApp's maybePop, never the root, and PopScope(canPop: false) refuses it (P4); a platform pushRouteInformation is answered by the first binding observer that returns true, else WidgetsApp pushes it by name through onGenerateRoute (P5), and an observer registered after WidgetsApp mounted comes too late (P5b); an unmounted Navigator detaches its observers and reports no pop of its routes (P6); a dialog is an observed push of an unnamed route and popUntil on a route identity pops it (P7); a page's Navigator.maybePop is an observed pop (P8); on the production binding runApp mounts the Navigator only after a timer, so microtasks run before it exists (P1). go_router 18.1.0 resolves on the pinned SDK and brings material_ui, cupertino_ui, flutter_localizations, intl, logging and flutter_web_plugins (R1); its push reaches the Navigator only after a frame (R2); it has no popUntil (R3); it navigates to the platform's initial route by itself (R4); go('/b') over [/, /a] leaves [/, /b] (R5). Fixtures against a stand-in nidana_dart_runtime_flutter, from a pure-Dart workspace root with the fixtures under hsdd/: structure 19 guarantees, 52 cases, 2 bindings; surface clean; 7 reject libraries, every code confirmed; this suite 52 of 52 and navigation-api@v1's executor suite 26 of 26 under fvm flutter test --no-pub; the name prefix 'G10 ' selected 8 cases; 33 seeded defects each failed the cases of the guarantee it breaks. Side finding (tool/widened_observe.dart, output-widened-observe.txt): the stand-in runtime types a subject by the static type of the first access, so reaching a topic through a Topic<Object?> reference and at its declared type on one bus throws a TypeError either way; bus-api@v1's fixtures always use the declared type.

notes_for_orchestrator: OQ-F1 is DECIDED in flutter-binding@v1 Refinement 1 (with G11 to G13 and G18): the executor and the module binding target Flutter's own Navigator through its imperative API and NavigatorObserver; no router package becomes a dependency. nidana.flutter's phase planning marks the OQ-F1 row RESOLVED pointing at flutter-binding@v1, and can sweep its Owns line 'against the router OQ-F1 selects' to 'over Flutter's Navigator'. Evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/flutter-binding-fixtures/ (P1 to P8, R1 to R5).

Bootstrap settled (Refinement 2, G12, G16): the router keeps its own stack and accepts performs before a Navigator hosts it, because runApp mounts the tree from a Timer (P1). Guide §3.5's order works unchanged: activate the nav-resolver, construct FlutterNavigationExecutor (and the ModuleScopeObserver), start(), then runApp(BusProvider(bus: bus, child: MaterialApp(navigatorKey: router.navigatorKey, navigatorObservers: [router.observer, modules], onGenerateInitialRoutes: router.initialRoutes, onGenerateRoute: router.generateRoute))).

For nidana.integration: the example app wires the router as above; its route builder must pass the RouteSettings it is given (G13, ArgumentError otherwise); platform deep links (the initial route and pushed routes) reach nav.intent as DeepLink by default (G15), so the app needs no deep-link capture of its own and must construct the executor before runApp; module references are released at the pop while the exit transition still runs, so a module whose pages read module-owned state during a Material exit transition (about 300 ms) needs a grace period longer than the 100 ms default; widget tests use WidgetTestBus (testing.dart) and pump t.wrap(page) as the root; the integration gate (--all) runs both flutter-binding bindings, nidana_dart_runtime_flutter_test.dart and flutter_navigation_executor_test.dart, under flutter test --no-pub.

For nidana.tooling's contracts (nidana-checks@v1): app code has a second claim site besides bus.publisher(..., writes:): PageScope(writes: {...}) claims those state topics at Scope.page through the adapter (G7), and PageScope(topologies:) and ModuleRoutes(topologies:) are activation sites of PAGE and MODULE topologies. The single-writer and scope-compatibility workspace scans should recognize them by package nidana_dart_runtime_flutter and element name, as bus-api@v1 'For static analysis' does for bus.publisher. The global-accessor check needs no change: BusProvider has no static accessor, and BusProvider.of(context) is the sanctioned path. WidgetTestBus.stub claims in test code, like TestBus.stub.

No existing contract needs a change for this one to stand. Optional follow-ups: (1) navigation-api@v1's Validation sentence that the stand-in Flutter binding was 'copied to where flutter-binding@v1's binding will live' can now name hsdd/contract/fixture/flutter-binding/behavior/flutter_navigation_executor_test.dart; its harness description (bus in the body, settle pumpAndSettle, elapse pump) holds as written. The binding constructs the executor before pumping its WidgetsApp, where S12's template pumped first; both orders pass. (2) bus-api@v1 candidate compatible addition: a case that reaches one topic both through a Topic<Object?> reference and at its declared type (for example a generic observe followed by getCurrentValue). The stand-in runtime throws a TypeError in both orders (tool/widened_observe.dart, output-widened-observe.txt in the experiment); nidana.runtime's design should key subjects by the topic's declared type, not the static type of the first access. flutter-binding@v1's own widgets observe at the declared type, so nothing here depends on it.

Decisions marked would_have_asked: OQ-F1 (axis: an owner with a web target or a go_router app might choose otherwise), module scope by stack membership (axis, Spec §7.3 silent), no shutdown at AppLifecycleState.detached (upstream), platform route forwarding on by default (axis, beyond the Owns list's wording), and the v1 exclusions, web URL sync above all (axis).

Upstream candidates (would_upstream): Guide §3.4's FlutterNavigationExecutor over GoRouter (go has route-tree semantics, push lands a frame later, no pop-until, go_router handles the platform's initial route past the bus guard, and 18.x depends on material_ui and cupertino_ui); Spec §7.3 is silent on stacked navigators (a covered module route); Spec §7.1 and §7.3 are silent on two mounted instances of one page topology (the React StrictMode note covers modules only); Spec §11.2's shutdown table has no Flutter row.

Timestamps are taken or file-evidence times: 20:10:21Z was taken when the design pass ended, before the probes; 20:16:47Z after the Navigator and go_router probes had run (OQ-F1 and the probe-informed decisions); 20:19:59Z is the executor binding's file time (fixture-convention decisions); 20:27:03Z is the file time of the module observer fix made after the first suite run showed the locked Navigator.
